platform_label: AWS c7i.48xlarge (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8488C, 192 logical CPUs, Linux)
caveats: Lockstep RTF: virtual time (min over RX streams) / wall time; RTF_min over complete 100 ms virtual windows (section 12.1).
Repetitions are shorter than the paced protocol of section 12.3 (>= 60 s, >= 1e4 pages); every point states its virtual time and pages.
The full product is pruned by the plan and by series pruning (see dropped.csv).
SIM benchmark geometry; LOS and RIS paths only (no ground, walls or diffuse).

F5 RTF is end-to-end (served engine's warm-up boundary to the RX client's last sample: computation, transport and client delivery); rtf_rx_client_median is the RX client's own figure (pre-fix metric, over-states a starved client), rtf_server_median the engine-only figure.
below_floor rows carry only a pilot RTF (sizing estimate), not a measured RTF.
Partial run: point filter features=['F4', 'F5'] points=None (64 of 909 plan points; the rest in dropped.csv).
F5 client processes ran on CPUs outside every slot (free cores; see slots.json client_cpus).

11 points ran concurrently, each pinned to 16 CPUs of whole cores in one NUMA node; concurrent points share L3, memory bandwidth and the power budget (see isolation.csv for the same points run alone).
Background load in meta.json includes the other concurrent points.

background_load.note: background_busy = system busy fraction minus this process's CPU share; child processes (MATLAB, ZMQ clients, controller processes, parallel point workers) count as background
